strategies.title:
Mechanism family: conflict-graph structural construction
Replacement scope: Repl
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: conflict-graph structural construction
Replacement scope: Replace `_greedy` inside `get_best_schedule` (keep `_local_search` and the time-budget wrapper); the multi-start loop now uses conflict-graph seeds instead of random starts.
Compute budget: One graph build per workload (O(n² key-compare via per-key transaction lists); up to ~10 seed constructions, each O(n log n); leaves ≥80% of the per-workload slice for local search. No new deadline pressure.
Gain mechanism: The incumbent greedy picks the locally cheapest append, which ignores global dependency structure: transactions sharing hot keys should be clustered so the simulator's optimizer can overlap their non-conflicting parts. Build a directed conflict graph (edge t→u if t must precede u for any reasonable serialization — i.e., they share a written key, with edge weight = conflict delay). Then (a) compute for each transaction a "conflict pressure" score (sum of incident conflict weights), and (b) construct seeds by repeatedly picking the transaction with highest pressure whose predecessors are already placed (topological order with pressure-based tie-breaking), which is a degree of freedom the greedy's myopic append cannot express. Feed each seed directly into the existing swap local search. Validity is preserved because any permutation is feasible; the graph only orders the seed, and the simulator's `get_opt_seq_cost` remains the sole judge. Falsifiable threshold: if the best-of-10 conflict-graph seeds + local search does not beat the incumbent's returned makespan on at least one of the three workloads, the mechanism is rejected.

strategies.title: Mechanism family: mesoscopic neighbourhood replacement (shift + adjacent-swap, f
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: mesoscopic neighbourhood replacement (shift + adjacent-swap, first-improvement)
Replacement scope: Replace `_local_search` (the swap hill-climb) with a shift-based local search: remove one transaction and reinsert it at the best of all n positions; also an adjacent-pair pass (cheap, O(n) evaluations per sweep).
Compute budget: One full shift sweep costs n² cost evaluations vs swap's n²; keep first-improvement with immediate restart of the sweep, deadline-checked every evaluation; cap to the same per-workload deadline slice as now.
Gain mechanism: Pairwise swaps often cannot escape local optima where a single transaction is simply in the wrong slot — moving one item to a distant position is a move no single swap can achieve in one step (it would need many consecutive improving swaps, each of which may individually raise cost). Shift-moves are exactly that missing degree of freedom. Adjacent-swap sweeps are retained as a cheap complementary pass since adjacent swaps are the most likely improving swaps and cost O(n) per sweep. Combine with the incumbent multi-start greedy for seeds. Feasibility invariant: shifts always yield a complete permutation, so validity is trivially preserved; cost is always recomputed by `get_opt_seq_cost`. Falsifiable threshold: on the incumbent's returned schedules, at least one improving shift move must exist that no single swap realizes; if the shift neighbourhood finds no improvement over the incumbent schedule on all three workloads, reject.

strategies.title:
Mechanism family: ruin-and-recreate structural exploration (LNS)
Replacement sco
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: ruin-and-recreate structural exploration (LNS)
Replacement scope: Replace the multi-start loop body in `get_best_schedule`: after one greedy construction + local search produces an incumbent, spend the remaining budget on repeated ruin-recreate cycles instead of fresh random-start greedies.
Compute budget: Ruin size k = max(3, n//10); each recreate is one greedy pass over k removed items reinserted greedily (k·n cost evaluations); deadline-checked per evaluation; keep the incumbent fallback schedule computed first. Same 300s shared deadline, split by /3 as now.
Gain mechanism: Multi-start greedy restarts from scratch and throws away all structure; LNS instead perturbs a good schedule by removing a cluster of related transactions (e.g., k transactions that share keys with a randomly chosen "hot" key — a topological perturbation, not a random restart), then greedily reinserts them optimally with the true cost function. This creates a coordinated multi-item move that neither swaps, shifts, nor independent restarts can express: it lets a whole conflicting group migrate to a better region of the schedule jointly. Accept only if the recreated schedule's true cost improves; otherwise keep the incumbent (fallback preserved). Validity: recreate always rebuilds a full permutation; all costs via `get_opt_seq_cost`. Falsifiable threshold: within the first 20 LNS iterations on workload 1, at least one accepted ruin-recreate must strictly lower the makespan below the multi-start-greedy incumbent; otherwise the mechanism shows no gain over the existing restart portfolio.

strategies.title: [permutation-stream-dp] Positional DP over transaction blocks
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: permutation-stream-dp (beam search over prefixes with true-cost pruning)
Replacement scope: Replace Stage 2 (multi-start greedy) in `get_best_schedule` with a beam search; keep Stage 1 seeds and Stage 3 local search as polish.
Compute budget: beam width ≤ 12, n=100 txns → ≤ 12·100 candidate expansions per level, each one memoized `_cost` call on a prefix; hard-deadline checked at each level. Falls back to incumbent greedy if beam exceeds its slice (~40% of this workload's deadline).
Gain mechanism: The incumbent greedy commits irrevocably to the single locally-best next transaction; a beam keeps W diverse partial prefixes alive and only collapses to one sequence at the end, so it can recover from a greedy trap that any single-path construction cannot. This is a genuinely different construction (set-of-prefixes DP), not a reparameterized greedy.
Plan: maintain a list of (prefix, cost) beams; at each step expand every beam with the ~W cheapest-to-append candidates (rank candidates by incremental cost `cost(prefix+[t]) - cost(prefix)`), deduplicate by prefix tuple, keep top W by true memoized cost. Seed the beam with the 5 highest-pressure transactions from `_build_conflict_graph`. Finish with `_local_search` on the best completed prefix. Validity: every beam element is a permutation prefix of distinct transaction IDs; completion is trivially a full permutation; the existing `best_seq` fallback guarantees a feasible return before deadline.
Expected-gain check: the new degree of freedom is surviving non-greedy prefixes; if greedy ever takes a wrong append (frequent when conflict delays are non-additive), the incumbent cannot recover while the beam can — falsifiable threshold: total makespan strictly below the incumbent's 251 (combined_score > 3968.25) on the same evaluation.

strategies.title: [segment-reorder-LNS] Ruin-and-recreate on contiguous segments
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: mesoscopic subsystem replacement (segment-extraction LNS with greedy reinsertion)
Replacement scope: Replace Stage 3 `_perturb` (random 2–3 reinsertions) with a segment-based LNS operator inside the same restart loop.
Compute budget: ≤ 25 LNS iterations; each iteration removes one contiguous segment of length 5–12 and reinserts its members greedily (≤ 12·n memoized cost evals), then one `_local_search` pass; hard deadline-checked per iteration.
Gain mechanism: The incumbent's perturbation scatters 2–3 isolated moves, which adjacent-swap/shift local search can largely already reach; extracting a whole contiguous segment and greedily rebuilding it reorders an interacting cluster of transactions simultaneously — a move outside the union of shift+2-opt+small-kick neighborhoods, so it can escape local optima the incumbent provably cannot.
Plan: pick a random window [i, i+L); remove those transactions; reinsert each one at the true-cost-best position in the remaining sequence (memoized `_cost`); accept only if the completed candidate's cost beats the incumbent, then run bounded `_local_search`. Keep the incumbent as fallback; every candidate is a full permutation by construction (remove-then-reinsert preserves the ID set).
Expected-gain check: the new move class is "simultaneous reordering of an interacting contiguous block", unreachable by the incumbent's ≤3 scattered reinsertions plus 2-opt — falsifiable threshold: any single-workload makespan improvement, i.e., total makespan < 251.

strategies.title: [insertion-order-scheduler] Earliest-conflict-first construction from pair-cost
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: structural construction via sampled true pair-cost precedence (replace conflict-graph heuristic weights with simulator-measured pair costs)
Replacement scope: Replace `_build_conflict_graph`'s structural set-overlap weights in Stage 1 with true simulator pair costs (as in Context 1's bounded pair sampling), and replace `_graph_seed`'s noisy-Kahn with a deterministic earliest-deadline-style construction: repeatedly append the transaction whose average pair cost against all unplaced transactions is lowest.
Compute budget: pair sampling capped at 80 memoized evaluations (~160 cost calls, most cached as 2-prefixes); construction is O(n²) table lookups, no simulator calls; Stage 1 slice unchanged (~45% of this workload's budget).
Gain mechanism: The incumbent's graph weights are heuristic proxies (write-write=1, read-write=0.5) that do not correspond to actual makespan cost; the true pair-cost table measures the real serialization delay the simulator charges, so seeds are built from measured conflict intensity rather than a guessed formula — a corrected bottleneck, and a different construction (average-measured-delay greedy) rather than a noise-based topological sort.
Plan: sample pairs (a,b) with the deterministic RNG, record `cost([a,b])` and `cost([b,a])` into an n×n table (symmetric fallback: average when unsampled); construction: at each step choose the unplaced transaction minimizing the mean of its table entries against remaining transactions; run 3 such seeds (tie-broken differently via slight table perturbation only in selection order, not in cost), then `_local_search` each. All candidates are permutations by construction; incumbent fallback preserved.
Expected-gain check: the corrected quantity is "true simulator pair cost" replacing fabricated 1.0/0.5 weights — the incumbent's seeds are ranked by a proxy the task statement explicitly warns does not track makespan; falsifiable threshold: total makespan < 251 on the shared evaluation, else the proxy weights were not the bottleneck.

strategies.title:
Mechanism family: beam-front-construction
Replacement scope: Replace Stage 2 (mu
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: beam-front-construction
Replacement scope: Replace Stage 2 (multi-start greedy loop) in `get_best_schedule`; keep Stage 1 seeds, Stage 3 perturbation, `_cost` cache, and `_local_search` unchanged.
Compute budget: Beam width 3–4, evaluated through the memoized `_cost` wrapper; one beam pass costs about (n candidates × width) cached prefix extensions per step, comparable to one greedy pass. Cap at 2 beam passes per workload within the existing stage-2 time slice; keep the shared deadline and incumbent fallback (identity permutation) for feasibility.
Gain mechanism: The incumbent greedy is irrevocably committed at each step — a locally bad-looking append can never be revisited, and its observed weakness is that only Stage-1 graph seeds provide diversity. A beam keeps the w best partial prefixes alive at each length (costed by the simulator's true `get_opt_seq_cost` on the partial sequence, so no heuristic bias is introduced), so it explores w construction paths the greedy can never reach; the best complete sequence from the beam then feeds the existing shift/2-opt local search. The new degree of freedom is parallel construction frontiers, which the incumbent's single-path greedy structurally cannot realize.
Plan: Maintain a list of beam nodes, each a (partial_seq, cached_true_cost). Initialize with the w structurally best seeds (top-pressure starts) plus one node per beam-slot from `_graph_seed`. At each depth, extend every beam node with every unplaced transaction, keep the w lowest-cost extensions (cost via `_cost(workload, node.seq + [t])`); prune duplicates by tuple key. When depth reaches n, take the best complete sequence, run `_local_search` under the stage deadline, and compare against the incumbent best_cost with the existing accept-only-if-better guard. Validity is inherent: every node is a partial permutation, extensions append only unused IDs, so the returned sequence is always a complete permutation of range(n); the existing assert and fallback stay in place.
Expected-gain check: The new degree of freedom is the multi-front construction (w=3–4 simultaneous prefixes) versus the incumbent's single irrevocable greedy path; if any beam frontier reaches a basin the greedy misses, the true makespan on at least one of the three workloads drops below the incumbent's, so the falsifiable threshold is total makespan < 251 (combined_score > 3968.25).

strategies.title:
Mechanism family: annealed-permutation
Replacement scope: Replace Stage 3 (`_per
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: annealed-permutation
Replacement scope: Replace Stage 3 (`_perturb` restarts) in `get_best_schedule` and the `_perturb` function; Stages 1–2, `_cost`, and deadline handling stay.
Compute budget: Deadline-bounded only (reuse the existing stage-3 slice); geometric cooling from T0 = 5% of incumbent cost to T_end = 0.1% over the slice, with swap/shift proposals evaluated via the memoized `_cost`; cache keeps repeated permutations free. No extra starts beyond what the slice allows.
Gain mechanism: The incumbent's Stage 3 accepts a candidate only if local search strictly beats the incumbent — it is monotone, so it is trapped in the basin of the greedy/graph-seed schedules; the observed makespan (251) has been frozen across several refinements (segment LNS, pair-cost tables all landed at 3968.25 or worse). Annealing's new degree of freedom is the acceptance of controlled worsening moves (probability exp(-Δ/T)), letting the walk cross ridges in the true-cost landscape that neither the 2-opt descent nor the bounded accept-only-if-better kicks can cross. Best-so-far is tracked separately, so the returned schedule is never worse than the entry incumbent.
Plan: Start from the incumbent best_seq. Loop until the slice deadline: propose either a random position swap or a random shift-insertion on the current sequence; compute c via `_cost`; if c <= current, accept; else accept with probability exp((current - c)/T) using the running temperature; every new best updates best_seq/best_cost; cool T multiplicatively each accepted move. On slice end, return the tracked best. Validity: proposals are permutation-preserving (swap two positions, or remove-and-reinsert one element), so every candidate is a full permutation; the best-so-far incumbent and the existing fallback guarantee a feasible return before the deadline.
Expected-gain check: The specific new transformation is non-monotone acceptance of true-cost-increasing swap/shift moves, which the incumbent's accept-only-if-better Stage 3 cannot execute; falsifiable threshold is total makespan < 251 (combined_score > 3968.25) on the fixed three-workload evaluation.

strategies.title:
Mechanism family: incumbent-polish
Replacement scope: Replace `_local_search`'s
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: incumbent-polish
Replacement scope: Replace `_local_search`'s neighborhood (add an or-opt pass: move contiguous segments of length 2–3 to any other position) and shift the stage budget split from 45/55 to 25/75 so more time goes to the proven greedy+local-search stage; everything else unchanged.
Compute budget: Or-opt adds O(n²) memoized evaluations per pass, bounded by the existing per-stage deadlines; stage split change only reallocates the same shared budget. No new starts.
Gain mechanism: The measured evidence is that the incumbent's Stage-1 graph seeds plus greedy+2-opt already dominate all attempted replacements (3968.25); the most credible remaining local gain is a strictly larger descent neighborhood — or-opt segment moves (length 2–3 block relocation) are not contained in the current shift (length-1) or 2-opt (swap) moves, so there are improving points the incumbent's descent provably cannot reach even though they are within one neighborhood step of the incumbent solution. This is the one allowed parameter/neighborhood polish of the incumbent.
Plan: In `_local_search`, after the existing shift pass and before the 2-opt pass, add a segment pass: for each segment length L in {2,3} and each start i, remove seq[i:i+L] and try inserting at every other position j (both orientations kept as block relocation), evaluating through `_cost`; apply best improvement and set the improved flag. Change the stage-1/2 split line from 0.45 to 0.25 so the greedy multi-start and the enriched local search get roughly double the time. All hard constraints are unchanged: candidates are complete permutations, best-so-far is kept, deadlines are checked inside every loop, and the identity fallback remains.
Expected-gain check: The new degree of freedom is the length-2–3 segment-relocation move, which is not a composition of any single incumbent move (one shift of length 1 or one pair swap); the falsifiable evaluator threshold is total makespan < 251, i.e., combined_score strictly above 3968.25, with no loss acceptable since the incumbent is retained as best-so-far.

Gain mechanism: The incumbent's Stage 3 accepts a candidate only if local search strictly beats the incumbent — it is monotone, so it is trapped in the basin of the greedy/graph-seed schedules; the observed makespan (251) has been frozen across several refinements (segment LNS, pair-cost tables all landed at 3968.25 or worse). Annealing's new degree of freedom is the acceptance of controlled worsening moves (probability exp(-Δ/T)), letting the walk cross ridges in the true-cost landscape that neither the 2-opt descent nor the bounded accept-only-if-better kicks can cross. Best-so-far is tracked separately, so the returned schedule is never worse than the entry incumbent.
Plan: Start from the incumbent best_seq. Loop until the slice deadline: propose either a random position swap or a random shift-insertion on the current sequence; compute c via `_cost`; if c <= current, accept; else accept with probability exp((current - c)/T) using the running temperature; every new best updates best_seq/best_cost; cool T multiplicatively each accepted move. On slice end, return the tracked best. Validity: proposals are permutation-preserving (swap two positions, or remove-and-reinsert one element), so every candidate is a full permutation; the best-so-far incumbent and the existing fallback guarantee a feasible return before the deadline.
Expected-gain check: The specific new transformation is non-monotone acceptance of true-cost-increasing swap/shift moves, which the incumbent's accept-only-if-better Stage 3 cannot execute; falsifiable threshold is total makespan < 251 (combined_score > 3968.25) on the fixed three-workload evaluation.

strategies.title: [population-crossover] Memetic recombination of diverse basin solutions
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: population-crossover
Replacement scope: Replace the Stage 2 + Stage 3 orchestration inside `get_best_schedule` (the beam-front block and the `_anneal` call); keep `_build_conflict_graph`/`_graph_seed`, `_cost`, and `_local_search` as reusable components.
Compute budget: Per workload slice (~100 s): population of 8, at most 30 generations; each generation produces 4 offspring via order crossover (OX) + one shift mutation each, followed by ONE capped `_local_search` pass (shift+2-opt only, no Or-opt) per offspring. All evaluations memoized via `_cost`; hard deadline checks before every generation and inside local search; incumbent fallback = best graph-seed result if budget expires.
Gain mechanism: The incumbent's restarts (graph seeds, beam, annealing) are memoryless — each restart explores its own basin and the best solutions found are never combined. Order crossover on two high-quality, structurally distinct schedules (enforce parent dissimilarity, e.g., Hamming/kendall distance above a threshold, picking parents tournament-style from the top half) recombines conflict-free ordering subsequences from different basins into a child neither single-trajectory method can reach. This is the classic memetic gain mechanism for permutation scheduling and is a genuinely new degree of freedom (inter-solution information transfer) rather than another single-walk escape move. Validity is structural: OX crossover and shift mutation both output complete permutations; assert `len(set(seq)) == n` before accepting.
Expected-gain check: The new degree of freedom is recombination of complementary orderings between distinct local optima, which no current stage possesses; falsifiable threshold — if the three-workload total makespan does not drop below the incumbent's 241 (i.e., combined_score does not exceed 4132.23), the mechanism is rejected.

strategies.title: [cluster-repair-lns] Hot-key conflict-clique destroy-and-repair
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: cluster-repair-lns
Replacement scope: Replace the `_anneal` Stage 3 call in `get_best_schedule` with a destroy-repair LNS loop operating on the incumbent best schedule; `_anneal` and its function body can be deleted.
Compute budget: Per workload: at most 40 destroy-repair rounds; each round destroys one cluster of at most 15 transactions and repairs by best-position reinsertion (≤ 15 × n memoized `_cost` calls, n = 100 → ≤ 1500 evaluations per round, most cache hits after early rounds). Accept only if the repaired schedule's true cost is strictly lower; keep incumbent otherwise. Hard deadline checks between rounds; the pre-LNS incumbent is always retained as fallback.
Gain mechanism: The incumbent's escape moves operate on single transactions (shift, swap) or contiguous position segments (Or-opt) — none of them can coherently relocate an entire conflict clique. Select the destroyed set structurally from the already-built conflict graph: rank keys by total incident conflict weight, take all transactions touching the top-1..3 hottest keys (plus graph-greedy growth up to 15 txns), remove them from the schedule, then reinsert them one at a time, each at the position (over all n−k remaining slots) minimizing the simulator's true cost. Because the removed set is a mutually conflicting group, the repair can re-time an entire hot-key interaction pattern at once — a set-valued, conflict-structured move that single-element neighborhoods cannot express (this is also distinct from the failed contiguous `segment-reorder-lns`, which reordered position-adjacent blocks with no conflict structure). Validity: removal + sequential reinsertion of all removed transactions always yields a complete permutation.
Expected-gain check: The new local transformation is coherent relocation of a whole hot-key conflict group with true-cost-guided reinsertion, which the incumbent's single-element and position-contiguous moves cannot realize; falsifiable threshold — if total makespan does not fall below 241 (combined_score above 4132.23), reject.

strategies.title: [regret-insertion] Mid-sequence regret construction replacing append-only beam
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: regret-insertion
Replacement scope: Replace the Stage 2 beam-front construction block in `get_best_schedule` (the `width = 4` beam loop) with a regret-insertion constructor; Stage 1 seeds and the post-construction `_local_search` polish are kept unchanged.
Compute budget: Per workload: single construction pass, n insertion steps; at each step evaluate at most 6 candidate transactions (top-6 by conflict `pressure`, ties broken randomly) at every current insertion position — ≤ 6 × k memoized `_cost` calls at step k, ≈ 6·n²/2 ≈ 30k calls worst case for n = 100, guarded by hard deadline checks every step with fallback to the Stage 1 best schedule. Construction followed by one `_local_search` pass to the stage deadline.
Gain mechanism: The incumbent's beam can only extend prefixes by appending at the end — its search topology is append-only, so a transaction misplaced early can never be inserted between two already-placed transactions during construction. The regret constructor builds the schedule by inserting each next transaction at ANY position of the partial schedule, choosing the candidate by regret (difference between its best and second-best insertion cost) so that transactions whose placement is most constrained go first. This is a different construction topology (arbitrary-position insertion vs. append) and a different selection criterion (true-cost regret vs. prefix-cost beam pruning). It is distinct from the failed `insertion-order-scheduler` family, which ordered transactions by a static heuristic pair-cost matrix with append-only sequencing and no simulator feedback; here every placement decision is judged by the simulator's true cost and the insertion position is itself a decision variable. Validity: each step inserts one not-yet-placed transaction into the partial permutation, so the result is structurally a complete permutation of all n transactions.
Expected-gain check: The new degree of freedom is mid-sequence insertion positions chosen by true-cost regret during construction, which the append-only beam cannot express; falsifiable threshold — if the constructor's polished schedule (plus the retained Stage 1/3 machinery) does not bring total makespan below 241 (combined_score above 4132.23), reject.

strategies.title:
Mechanism family: layered-block-partition
Replacement scope: Replace Stage 2 (re
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: layered-block-partition
Replacement scope: Replace Stage 2 (regret-insertion construction) in `get_best_schedule`; keep Stage 1 seeds, local search, and annealing as polish.
Compute budget: Structural partition build is O(n²) set work (free, no simulator calls); the block-order search uses at most ~200 memoized `_cost` calls on block-order permutations (n_blocks ≤ ~15, so full or sampled orderings of blocks are cheap); remaining slice budget unchanged. Expected effect: construction finishes in <20s, leaving more time for annealing/local search than the incumbent's regret stage.
Gain mechanism: The incumbent treats all 100 transactions as one flat permutation space; the true bottleneck is hot keys serializing large groups. Partition transactions into layers by shared-key conflict graph: compute connected components/cliques on write-key overlap, order components by structural conflict weight, and within each component order by the existing conflict-pressure heuristic. Then optimize the *block order* (permutations of whole blocks) with true-cost evaluation — a search space the incumbent never explores, because its shift/2-opt moves break blocks apart. A final intra-block local search restores full-neighborhood refinement. This gives a genuinely different construction topology (grouped subsystems) and a new degree of freedom (block-level ordering) the flat search cannot reach efficiently.
Plan: (1) Build write-key → transaction index; group transactions sharing any write key into blocks via union-find, then merge small blocks greedily until ≤15 blocks. (2) Order blocks by descending total conflict weight (sum of pairwise weights between blocks from `_build_conflict_graph`); order within block by pressure. (3) Enumerate/sample block orderings (all if ≤8 blocks, else greedy insertion of blocks evaluated by `_cost`), keep best. (4) Hand the best full permutation to existing `_local_search` then `_anneal`. Fallback: if partitioning yields one giant block, fall back to the incumbent's regret construction unchanged. Validity: output is always a complete permutation; deadline-checked at every enumeration step; incumbent best_seq fallback retained.
Expected-gain check: New degree of freedom is block-order optimization over a search space the flat shift/2-opt neighborhood cannot traverse without destroying block structure; falsifiable threshold: total makespan < 231 (combined_score > 4310.34) on the evaluator.

strategies.title:
Mechanism family: prefix-beam-true-cost
Replacement scope: Replace Stage 2's reg
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: prefix-beam-true-cost
Replacement scope: Replace Stage 2's regret-insertion loop entirely with a beam search over prefixes; keep Stages 1 and 3.
Compute budget: Beam width k=8, one step per transaction (100 steps), ≤ k·n candidate extensions per step but pruned to k·8 true-cost evaluations via the memoized `_cost` on prefixes; hard deadline check every step. Expected effect: comparable evaluation count to regret insertion but with global lookahead instead of myopic per-step regret.
Gain mechanism: The incumbent's regret insertion commits each chosen transaction permanently at the single globally cheapest position, a myopic greedy that cannot reconsider; the observed 231-makespan solutions come from this single committed trajectory plus local repair. A beam keeps k diverse partial prefixes alive, evaluated by true cost, so early mistakes (which local search later cannot undo because they're buried mid-sequence) are avoided. This is a different construction mechanism (parallel partial-schedule exploration with pruning), not a parameter change.
Plan: (1) Seed the beam with the 8 highest-pressure transactions as length-1 prefixes (or with the Stage-1 seed's first 8 elements). (2) At each step, for each beam member, extend with the 6 most-conflicting unplaced transactions (by pairwise weight to the placed set); evaluate each extension prefix with `_cost`; keep global top-k distinct prefixes. (3) When complete, take the best full permutation, run `_local_search` then `_anneal` on it with remaining budget. (4) Deadline checks at every inner loop; if the beam stalls past deadline, complete the best prefix by appending remaining transactions in pressure order and cost it. Validity: every returned sequence is a complete permutation; incumbent fallback preserved.
Expected-gain check: The new degree of freedom is maintaining k alternative prefix trajectories with true-cost pruning, which the single-trajectory regret constructor structurally lacks; falsifiable threshold: total makespan ≤ 229 (combined_score > 4347) on the evaluator.

strategies.title:
Mechanism family: anneal-reheat-cycles
Replacement scope: Replace `_anneal`'s si
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: anneal-reheat-cycles
Replacement scope: Replace `_anneal`'s single monotone cooling schedule and its invocation in Stage 3; everything else unchanged.
Compute budget: Same Stage-3 slice; 3 reheat cycles within it, each cycle's T0 shrinking geometrically (3% → 1% → 0.3% of incumbent cost), each followed by a short `_local_search` polish (shift pass only, deadline-checked). No new simulator-start budget — same total evaluations, redistributed.
Gain mechanism: The incumbent's single monotone cooling pass spends most of its slice at temperatures too low to escape the incumbent basin (T decays to 0.05% quickly given the ~3000 it/s horizon). Reheat cycles restart exploration at progressively lower temperatures, each seeded from the polished best-so-far — a "iterated local search with thermal restarts" escape direction that single-pass cooling cannot realize. This is the one allowed parameter/topology-polish strategy, but the reheat cycle is a structural change to the annealing trajectory, not a tolerance tweak.
Plan: (1) Split the Stage-3 deadline into 3 equal sub-slices. (2) For each sub-slice, run the existing annealing loop with T0 = f_i · best_cost (f = 0.03, 0.01, 0.003), T_end = 0.0005·best_cost, same swap/shift proposals. (3) After each sub-slice, run one shift-pass-only `_local_search` polish on the returned best. (4) Track global best across cycles; return it. Validity: best-so-far tracking guarantees no regression vs. the Stage-2 incumbent; permutation-preserving moves only.
Expected-gain check: The new degree of freedom is the multi-cycle reheat trajectory (three temperature restarts with interleaved descent) versus one monotone cooling pass; falsifiable threshold: total makespan ≤ 230 (combined_score ≥ 4329) on the evaluator, else reject.

strategies.title: [ruin-recreate-lns] Destroy-and-rebuild large segments with regret insertion
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: ruin-recreate-lns
Replacement scope: Replace Stage 3 (`_anneal` call plus final polish in `get_best_schedule`) with a large-neighborhood ruin-and-recreate loop; keep Stages 1–2 and `_local_search` unchanged.
Compute budget: Up to ~40 LNS iterations within the remaining slice; each iteration removes a random contiguous window of 15–25 transactions (or a key-cluster set) and reinserts them greedily via the memoized `_cost` at every position, then one `_local_search` pass. Deadline-checked per candidate; expected evaluation time unchanged (same 300s shared budget).
Gain mechanism: The incumbent's annealer proposes single-element swaps/shifts, which cannot reorganize a contiguous block of mutually-conflicting transactions into a better collective arrangement — removing k transactions at once and reinserting each at its globally best position is a degree of freedom (block relocation) the Metropolis single-move walk realizes only through many coordinated accepted moves, each of which is usually rejected. Validity is structural: every candidate is a full permutation built by insertion of the removed set, and best-so-far tracking with the Stage-2 incumbent as fallback guarantees never returning worse than the current parent. Expected-gain check: if any single LNS rebuild finds a permutation with true makespan below the incumbent's 231-sum, the evaluator score strictly exceeds 4310.34; falsifiable threshold: total makespan ≤ 230.

strategies.title: [key-cluster-blocks] Group transactions by shared-key clusters as an atomic orde
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: key-cluster-blocks
Replacement scope: Replace Stage 2's regret-insertion construction (the partial-schedule insertion loop) with a two-level construction: cluster transactions via connected components of the conflict graph (union-find on key overlap, merging until clusters have ≤ ~12 members), order transactions within each cluster by exhaustive/beam search using `_cost`, then order the cluster blocks themselves by regret insertion evaluated at block granularity.
Compute budget: Cluster build is O(n²) set intersections (free). Within-cluster ordering: beam of width 4 over ≤12 transactions (~hundreds of memoized `_cost` calls per cluster). Block-level regret insertion: O(k²) calls for k clusters. All inside the existing 70% stage slice; no change to total evaluation time.
Gain mechanism: The incumbent treats all n transactions as an undifferentiated permutation, so local search must move each member of a hot-key clique individually even though the clique's internal order is what determines its serialization cost. Clustering makes the clique's internal order an explicit optimized subsystem (small enough to near-optimally solve) while the block-level search handles the coarse structure — a mesoscopic decomposition the flat representation cannot express. Every candidate remains a complete permutation (blocks are concatenated lists of transaction IDs); incumbent fallback is the Stage-1 best if the deadline hits mid-construction. Expected-gain check: the new degree of freedom is near-optimal intra-clique ordering, which flat shift/2-opt local search demonstrably under-optimizes on hot-key cliques; falsifiable evaluator threshold: total makespan ≤ 230 (score > 4310.34).

Replacement scope: Replace `_anneal`'s proposal distribution and initial state: seed the annealer from a deterministic layout built by sorting transactions by descending pressure and grouping write-heavy transactions to adjacent positions, and add a third proposal type — reverse a random contiguous segment of length 3–8 (segment inversion).
Compute budget: Same annealing slice as now (all remaining time after Stage 2, ~3000 it/s estimated horizon); segment inversion costs one memoized `_cost` call per proposal, identical to current proposals. No new starts beyond the current single anneal run.
Gain mechanism: Segment inversion is a geometrically different escape direction: it reverses the relative order of a whole conflicting run in one move, which the incumbent's pair-swap/shift proposals cannot do without a chain of individually-rejected intermediate states. The pressure-sorted, write-grouped seed places write-write conflicting transactions near each other so inversions explore their orderings cheaply. This is the one parameter-plus-proposal polish of the incumbent optimizer in the portfolio. Validity is structural (inversions preserve permutation); best-so-far tracking plus the entry incumbent as fallback guarantee no regression. Expected-gain check: the new move class (segment inversion) is unavailable to the incumbent's proposal set, so any accepted inversion improving the true cost yields makespan < 231 sum; falsifiable threshold: total makespan ≤ 230 on the evaluator.

strategies.title: ordered attempt [ruin-recreate-lns] Destroy-and-rebuild large segments with regret insertion
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: ruin-recreate-lns
Replacement scope: Replace Stage 3 (`_anneal` call plus final polish in `get_best_schedule`) with a large-neighborhood ruin-and-recreate loop; keep Stages 1–2 and `_local_search` unchanged.
Compute budget: Up to ~40 LNS iterations within the remaining slice; each iteration removes a random contiguous window of 15–25 transactions (or a key-cluster set) and reinserts them greedily via the memoized `_cost` at every position, then one `_local_search` pass. Deadline-checked per candidate; expected evaluation time unchanged (same 300s shared budget).
Gain mechanism: The incumbent's annealer proposes single-element swaps/shifts, which cannot reorganize a contiguous block of mutually-conflicting transactions into a better collective arrangement — removing k transactions at once and reinserting each at its globally best position is a degree of freedom (block relocation) the Metropolis single-move walk realizes only through many coordinated accepted moves, each of which is usually rejected. Validity is structural: every candidate is a full permutation built by insertion of the removed set, and best-so-far tracking with the Stage-2 incumbent as fallback guarantees never returning worse than the current parent. Expected-gain check: if any single LNS rebuild finds a permutation with true makespan below the incumbent's 231-sum, the evaluator score strictly exceeds 4310.34; falsifiable threshold: total makespan ≤ 230.

strategies.title: ordered attempt [key-cluster-blocks] Group transactions by shared-key clusters as an atomic orde
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: key-cluster-blocks
Replacement scope: Replace Stage 2's regret-insertion construction (the partial-schedule insertion loop) with a two-level construction: cluster transactions via connected components of the conflict graph (union-find on key overlap, merging until clusters have ≤ ~12 members), order transactions within each cluster by exhaustive/beam search using `_cost`, then order the cluster blocks themselves by regret insertion evaluated at block granularity.
Compute budget: Cluster build is O(n²) set intersections (free). Within-cluster ordering: beam of width 4 over ≤12 transactions (~hundreds of memoized `_cost` calls per cluster). Block-level regret insertion: O(k²) calls for k clusters. All inside the existing 70% stage slice; no change to total evaluation time.
Gain mechanism: The incumbent treats all n transactions as an undifferentiated permutation, so local search must move each member of a hot-key clique individually even though the clique's internal order is what determines its serialization cost. Clustering makes the clique's internal order an explicit optimized subsystem (small enough to near-optimally solve) while the block-level search handles the coarse structure — a mesoscopic decomposition the flat representation cannot express. Every candidate remains a complete permutation (blocks are concatenated lists of transaction IDs); incumbent fallback is the Stage-1 best if the deadline hits mid-construction. Expected-gain check: the new degree of freedom is near-optimal intra-clique ordering, which flat shift/2-opt local search demonstrably under-optimizes on hot-key cliques; falsifiable evaluator threshold: total makespan ≤ 230 (score > 4310.34).

strategies.title: [beam-construction] True-cost parallel beam construction over insertion states
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: beam-construction
Replacement scope: Stage 2 of `get_best_schedule` (the regret-insertion loop) — keep Stage 1 graph seeds and Stage 3 anneal/polish intact.
Compute budget: Beam width W=8, one expansion step per unplaced transaction, each state evaluated via memoized `_cost`; cap total step count at n and give Stage 2 the same ~70% mid-stage slice it has now. Cache makes per-step cost ~O(W·k·positions) evaluations; with memoization most prefixes repeat across steps, so wall-clock stays within the current stage budget (falsifiable: if Stage 2 exceeds its slice, fall back to the incumbent regret solution already computed in Stage 1).
Gain mechanism: Regret insertion is a single-path greedy — one bad early placement poisons the whole permutation, and only local search (shift/2-opt/anneal) can repair it afterward. A beam keeps W distinct partial orderings alive, so a locally painful-but-globally-good early placement survives in a sibling state instead of being committed irrevocably. Specifically: at each step, maintain a set of (partial_permutation, cost) states; for each state, for each of the top-m (m=4, by structural pressure) unplaced transactions, evaluate appending/inserting it at the best position; prune to the W best (cost, diversity-shuffled) states. Diversity guard: reject a new state whose transaction set equals an existing state's and whose permutation is a shift of it. Final complete states feed the existing `_local_search` + `_anneal`. Validity is trivially preserved: every state is a partial permutation extended one transaction at a time; the terminal state is a complete permutation, and the incumbent fallback (`best_seq = list(range(n))`) remains. Expected-gain check: the new degree of freedom is parallel non-greedy construction paths, which the incumbent's single-path regret loop cannot realize; if any beam state beats the incumbent's regret construction on even one of the three workloads, the summed makespan strictly drops below the current 230 total, which is directly falsifiable in the evaluator.

strategies.title: [simulator-calibrated-graph] Replace structural conflict weights with empiricall
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: simulator-calibrated-graph
Replacement scope: `_build_conflict_graph`'s weight/pressure computation (the `ww + 0.5*(aw+bw)` heuristic weights), plus the ranking constants used in `_graph_seed` and the Stage-2 candidate ordering; the downstream search machinery is untouched.
Compute budget: Calibration pass of at most ~300 simulator calls (memoized, small prefixes: pairs placed adjacent in both orders plus a few sampled contexts), performed inside the existing Stage-1 graph slice (< 2 s); everything else reuses the current deadlines. The calibration calls are cached in `_cost_cache`, so any prefix reused later is free.
Gain mechanism: The incumbent's conflict weights (write-write = 1.0, read-write = 0.5) are arbitrary guesses about how much a shared key actually delays the schedule; the observed evidence is that pressure-based seeds and regret candidate ordering are the weakest remaining components (structural-heuristic families like key-cluster-blocks and cluster-repair all scored well below the incumbent, suggesting the structural signal is misweighted, not under-searched). Calibration: sample transaction pairs (a,b) that conflict, query `_cost` on small contexts [a,b,...] vs [b,a,...] to estimate the true pairwise delay in each direction; fit a single per-feature linear model delay ≈ α·ww + β·rw_forward + γ·rw_backward (3–4 parameters, least squares on the ~300 samples). Use the fitted α, β, γ in the graph weights, pressure, and `_graph_seed` tie-breaking. This changes only the guide function, never the cost oracle, so all moves remain permutations and validity constraints are untouched. Expected-gain check: the new degree of freedom is direction-sensitive, data-calibrated conflict weights (current model is symmetric in read direction and uses invented constants); it is falsifiable by comparing the calibrated model's predicted pair delays against held-out `_cost` samples and by whether Stage-1/Stage-2 seeds reach lower true cost than the incumbent's seeds within the same slice.

strategies.title: [ejection-chain-descent] Lin–Kernighan-style ejection-chain local search replaci
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: ejection-chain-descent
Replacement scope: The body of `_local_search` (shift + Or-opt + 2-opt passes) is replaced by an ejection-chain descent; `_anneal` and all construction stages are unchanged, and the ejection chain runs in the same local-search time slices.
Compute budget: Each descent starts from the incumbent; chain depth capped at 10 ejections; per chain step, only the best of ~n candidate insertions is evaluated (best-improvement on a single chain, not exhaustive passes). Total per restart ≤ ~10·n memoized `_cost` calls; run repeatedly (multistart from perturbed incumbents) until the local-search deadline slice expires. This is asymptotically cheaper than the incumbent's full O(n²) 2-opt sweeps, so more improvement moves fit in the same slice.
Gain mechanism: The incumbent's local search accepts only single improving moves — shift, segment relocate, or a pairwise swap — so any reordering that requires temporarily increasing cost (e.g., pulling a hot transaction out of position i, cascading the displaced transaction to position j, which pushes a third transaction to a position that only then becomes beneficial) is unreachable except via the annealing stage's slow random walk. An ejection chain realizes exactly this: remove the transaction at a seed position, reinsert it at its best position, the displaced transaction is ejected and reinserted at its best position, and so on up to depth 10; the chain is accepted only if the cumulative (final) cost improves, and every intermediate state is a valid permutation (remove-and-reinsert always keeps the multiset of transaction IDs). Direction: seed the chain at the positions where the conflict graph says the incumbent has the highest incident delay (reuse the existing `weight` matrix). The incumbent fallback and final anneal remain, so the returned schedule is never worse than the entry incumbent. Expected-gain check: the new degree of freedom is compound depth-k moves with intermediate cost increases accepted by construction, which flat shift/2-opt cannot make in one improving step; the falsifiable threshold is whether ejection-chain descent, given the same time slice as the incumbent's `_local_search`, returns a strictly lower true cost on at least one of the three workloads (sum < current 230).
